messages:
irene: Heads-up — nightly SAST run flagged 18 findings in infra repo. Most are secret-detection hits that look like KMS ARNs inside terraform templates. Suspect false positives from our modules; they’re flooding the security queue. Can we tweak the suppression/triage flow?

alex: can you paste one of the raw findings? want to confirm it’s just the ARN pattern and not an embedded secret.

irene: here’s an example copy-paste from the SAST output:
```text
Rule: secret-detection
Severity: medium
File: infra/modules/kms/variables.tf
Match: "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01-2345"
Context: variable "kms_key_arn" { default = "arn:aws:kms:..." }
```

alex: yep looks like pattern-based hits. Two options: 1) add a repo-level allowlist for recognized KMS ARN templates, 2) refine the detector to ignore full ARNs but still catch embedded base64 secrets. Preference for (2) long-term.

sam: agree on refining detector. In the meantime we should avoid blanket suppressions. My proposal: automatic hush rule if the finding matches exact regex for aws:kms ARN AND the file path is under infra/modules (we trust those modules). But require an audit label so we log who approved the hush.

maya: small RBAC note — security needs read access to CloudTrail logs across infra accounts to verify whether a key was used. Can we add a cross-account role with CloudTrailReadOnly and KMSDescribe permissions? That would be least-privileged.

alex: yes — propose adding a terraform module in infra repo that creates a role: sts:AssumeRole by security SSO group, with policies: cloudtrail:LookupEvents, s3:GetObject (for CT buckets), kms:DescribeKey. Will open a draft PR.

irene: SGTM. Also: we should record any hush decision in the scan audit so we can re-evaluate after model/rule updates. Add a metadata tag in the scan result like `approved_by=irene` and `reason=known-kms-arn-template`.

sam: +1. I'll update the triage playbook to require: owner (team), severity, justification, and expiration (30d) for any auto-suppression. If the finding persists after expiration it must be re-reviewed.

deploy-bot: DAST report uploaded: staging found exposed endpoint `/internal/debug` (status 200). See: https://ci.internal/reports/dast/176760/

alex: oh — that endpoint should be disabled in non-local builds. quick mitigation: block via nginx for staging and add unit test to fail CI if any /internal/* endpoints are reachable from public.

irene: simple curl to reproduce: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" https://staging.internal/api/internal/debug` returned 200 for me.

maya: agreed — add pre-deploy check. Also add a hardening checklist item: ensure debug endpoints are behind allowlist or only enabled for local dev.

sam: action items I’ll take: update triage playbook (doc link: https://confluence.internal/security/triage-playbook), add auto-expire metadata, and add sample regex for KMS ARN hush.

alex: I’ll open PR for the cross-account role module and a small change to the SAST config to add the interim hush rule limited to infra/modules paths. PR link: (will post when ready).

irene: sounds good. After PRs land can we run a smoke SAST to confirm noise drops under 5 items?

maya: yes — and I’ll add CloudTrail read role to the security SSO group once the module PR is merged.

irene: perfect. tagging owners: @alex to PR infra role, @sam to update triage playbook, @maya to handle CloudTrail RBAC. Thanks all :thumbsup:

alex: noted. I’ll target a PR by EOD tomorrow.

sam: will have playbook update by EOD as well.

deploy-bot: deploy pipeline: new job `predeploy-harden` will be added to fail on reachable /internal endpoints (planned).
